finding: "Nothing is emitted and no state is written" is not buildable at the point where the deactivation set becomes known. Both commands write the round-N spec snapshot BEFORE role resolution: tp review calls loadReviewRoundState (review.go:358 -> WriteSnapshotAtomic at review.go:1629) and only then buildReviewPrompts (review.go:397), which is where ResolveActiveCorpus/ResolveOverrideFocus run; tp audit calls loadAuditSpec (audit.go:196 -> WriteSnapshotAtomic at audit.go:371) and resolves roles at audit.go:234. A refusal raised where the disabled set is known therefore leaves snapshot-round-N.md on disk, which engine.InFlightRound reports as an interrupted round to --status and tp resume. Test 7 ("emits nothing, and writes no state") cannot pass without a reordering the spec never mentions.

finding: Both refusals are stated at command granularity ("`tp review` and `tp audit` refuse it", "the command exits 2") without naming which invocation modes are covered. `tp review` is one command with many modes (default emission, --record, --status, --merge, --resolve/--resolve-all, --verify, --report), and `tp audit` likewise (--record, --status, --merge). finding: "an unresolved review finding" is left undefined, and tp already has a conflicting definition. engine.reviewFindingResolvedAway (internal/engine/reviewclean.go:32) treats a recorded row as out of the surviving set ONLY when resolved.status is wontfix or duplicate AND resolved.evidence is non-empty; a row resolved fixed still survives, and a wontfix row with empty evidence still survives. So "unresolved" could mean (a) no resolved block at all, (b) not resolved-away per the existing predicate, or (c) anything that dirties a round per parseRecordRows (review_record.go:212-214, where duplicate dirties but wontfix-with-evidence does not). The three readings disagree on real rows, and the choice decides whether an exit-2 refusal fires.

finding: Scoping the check to "the latest recorded round of that phase" leaves the guard trivially bypassable, and no §7 item probes it. A role's rows live in the round file it wrote them into; if the role contributes no row to round N+1 — because it was skipped that round (no-checklist-items, no-spec-change, domain-mismatch) or simply reported nothing new — its still-open rows from round N are invisible to a latest-round-only scan, and `enabled: false` then succeeds while open findings stay in recorded state. That is precisely the failure §2.6 exists to prevent, reached in one extra round instead of zero. The spec also does not say what happens when the latest recorded round for the phase is an in-flight round (snapshot written, no <phase>-round-N.ndjson recorded yet — the existing in_flight_round state).

finding: §2.6 scopes the unresolved-findings refusal to 'the latest recorded round of that phase', justifying it by 'the prior-round carry mechanism re-presents a role's own unresolved rows in its next-round prompt'. finding: The release exists to save tokens and never states the arithmetic. v0.31.2 §6 set the in-repo precedent of a per-role cost table, and it raised the per-role price this feature lets a project decline: every shared-arm audit prompt now carries a `## Project Context` block (up to 50 lines) plus the `## Disposition` paragraph, so a declined auditor is now worth roughly +55 preamble lines, up to `CodeFileCap` (10) named files the sub-agent reads itself, one result row per file the driver must produce/merge/read, and one whole sub-agent invocation — multiplied by the required clean rounds. The evidence in §1 is also asymmetric: the only measured datum (3 project-authored roles → 38 of 92 findings, one shared cluster) supports keeping roles on, while the deactivation case ('two lenses are the highest-value ones and the rest are noise') is an unmeasured report. finding: §2.3, §2.5 and §2.6 can all fire on one invocation and their precedence is unstated. Two concrete cases. (a) §2.3 makes `enabled: false` on an id matching no active role a warn-and-ignore; §2.6 refuses deactivation of a role carrying unresolved rows. A role can hold unresolved rows in recorded state while no longer being active — its file was deleted, or a domains/domain edit filtered it out — so both rules describe the same input and give opposite answers (warn and continue vs exit 2). (b) When deactivating the last role of a phase also happens to deactivate a role with unresolved findings, §2.5 and §2.6 both apply and the spec does not say which error the driver sees. Deterministic errors are a stated tp property; two rules racing for one exit make the message non-deterministic across implementations.

The scan covers EVERY recorded round rather than the latest, closing the bypass where a role that contributed nothing to round N hides its round N-1 rows, and matching what loadReviewRoundState actually carries for review. The refusal now names the recorded round file each unresolved item lives in, which is what makes the escape hatch reachable — resolving the merged working file never touches recorded state.

finding: §5 asks `skills/tp/SKILL.md` to carry the full semantics of both refusals. SKILL.md bytes are the most expensive bytes in the project — they load into every agent session unconditionally, whether or not that session ever writes an `enabled: false`. Both refusals are self-announcing at the moment they matter: §2.5 and §2.6 each exit 2 with an error naming the phase or role and a hint pointing at the fix, which is tp's own stated AX mechanism for this ('clear actionable errors with hint field'). Paying per-session context for a rule that the error already delivers at point of need is the pattern this project treats as waste elsewhere.

suggestion: Split the doc burden by cost: SKILL.md states the two permitted keys and the `disabled-by-spec` reason in the existing frontmatter block (a line or two); REFERENCE.md carries both refusals in full, as the lookup document; and the exit-2 hints stay the primary delivery. Keep CLAUDE.md's role-corpus rule to the one-sentence `domains`-vs-`enabled` distinction.

finding: Non-Goal 4 justifies rejecting project-level deactivation with 'Turning a role off for every spec is already expressible: delete or stop committing its file', and §3's proposed advice repeats it ('deleting the role file removes it from every spec'). That holds only while at least one file remains in the phase directory: LoadRoleCorpus reports the phase unpopulated when .tp/<phase>/ is empty or absent, and ResolveActiveCorpus then returns the domain-selected embedded default corpus. Deleting the last role file therefore does not turn the role off — it silently restores the full embedded default panel the project had replaced.

finding: Item 1 asserts the role is removed "from the emitted panel". "Panel" is tp's prose word for the active role set, not an output field; the emission JSON exposes the prompts array (reviewPrompt/auditPrompt entries keyed by `role`), plus `skipped_roles`. Two engineers assert different things — one that no prompt entry has role == X, one that some role-count summary shrank. Item 2's "anywhere in the emitted output" has the same looseness, though substring absence makes it recoverable.
